sections.content: This lesson doesn't teach new grammar: it combines the structures you've already met — the van/vannak existential verb for location, the mellett/mentén/között postpositions, the -ból/-ből áll structure, and the határos + compass-direction pattern — into longer, more natural sentences, exactly the way you'd use them in a real self-introduction or at a naturalization interview.

items.spanish: Magyarország Közép-Európában, a Kárpát-medencében fekszik, és hét országgal határos.
items.english: Hungary lies in Central Europe, in the Carpathian Basin, and borders seven countries.

items.spanish: A főváros, Budapest, a Duna mellett van, az ország pedig tizenkilenc megyéből áll.
items.english: The capital, Budapest, is beside the Danube, and the country consists of nineteen counties.

items.spanish: Északra Szlovákia, délre Szerbia és Horvátország található.
items.english: To the north is Slovakia; to the south are Serbia and Croatia.

sections.content: A good summary sentence draws on several structures at once: a van/fekszik for the location, a postposition for the details, a -ból/-ből áll for the composition. Practice this combination — it's exactly the kind of sentence you'd produce if someone asked you: 'Tell me a little about Hungary.'
